free_tier.stated: KRW 300,000 of credit for new customers who register a payment method and apply within three months of signup, usable against most services. Outbound data is free up to 30 GiB a month.

chaining: KRW 300,000 against a KRW-denominated 2 vCPU instance is several months of a small box, but the whole chain sits behind a Korean business registration number.

limits.value: Signup itself requires a business registration certificate (saeopja-deungnokjeung) and a business registration number, so an individual outside Korea cannot open the account that holds the credit.

identity_cost.detail: a registered business is required before signup: the signup guide states a copy of the Korean business registration certificate (saeopja-deungnokjeung) must be prepared and that uploading it with its registration number is a mandatory first step, so the account needs a legal entity rather than a person's ID document; the KRW 300,000 credit then needs a payment method registered and an application within three months of signup. No hold is stated and debit or prepaid acceptance is not stated; the startup tracks, KRW 5,000,000 for a year and KRW 35,000,000 over two, need the same entity

evidence.proved: the new-signup programme page states, in Korean, that a credit worth KRW 300,000 is granted to a customer who applies within 3 months of signup, usable against payment for various services, and lists the two steps as registering a payment method and then applying for the credit

the signup guide states, in Korean, that a copy of the business registration certificate must be prepared before signup, and that uploading the business registration certificate and entering its registration number is a mandatory first step of the KakaoCloud signup procedure

the startup programme blog states, in Korean, that the Launch track gives KRW 5,000,000 of credit usable for one year to every qualified startup, and that the Grow track gives KRW 35,000,000 over two years to companies backed by a partner VC or accelerator
the cheapest Korean plan in the index is KakaoCloud t1i.nano at 2 vCPU and 0.5 GB for USD 2.98 a month with outbound 30 GiB free; a third-party price comparison, reported not documented

notes: This refutes the common English roundup line that KakaoCloud is a cheap Korean cloud anyone can open: the gate is a business licence, not a phone. The startup track (KRW 5,000,000 for a year) is larger and needs a legal entity but no revenue.
